one_month_reasoning: No Salesforce earnings fall in the window. Q2 FY27 was reported on 2026-08-26, and Q3 FY27 normally comes in early December. Dreamforce and Investor Day (Sep 16) are already past. Events inside the window: the final ASR settlement, expected in October (about 34M more shares at the $182 expected average; already known); the closing of the Contentful ($1.5B) and Fin ($3.6B) deals, which guidance already includes; and late-October peer and hyperscaler earnings (ServiceNow, Microsoft) plus the FOMC. None of these is a strong directional catalyst. The stock has also come off a $268 intraday high on 2026-09-03 to $225-231, so momentum and reversal signals roughly cancel. I use a near-symmetric lognormal with median about $231.8 (a tiny tilt for the settlement share count) and monthly sigma of 0.132 (about 47% annual vol / 3.5). This is essentially unchanged from round 1, and the supervisor agreed with it.

fair_value.method: Two methods weighted equally on Sep-2027 NTM estimates (NTM = 1/3 FY28 + 2/3 FY29). (1) 14.5x NTM core EPS of about $17.7 (FY28 about $16.3, FY29 about $18.4, no investment gains) gives $257. (2) SBC-adjusted NTM FCF of about $12.5B ($17.3B FCF less $4.8B SBC at about 9% of revenue) over about 783M shares is $16.0/share; at a 6.25% yield that gives $255. The blend is about $256 (round 1: $266).

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Sep-2027 NTM core EPS of about $17.7 = 1/3 x FY28 $16.3 + 2/3 x FY29 $18.4, x 14.5x. FY28 = FY27 core net income of about $11.5B (13.7 x 838M) grown about 10%, giving $12.6B, over about 783M average diluted shares. FY29 = net income +11% and shares -1.5%.

inputs_detail.input: FY27 core EPS excluding strategic-investment gains
inputs_detail.derivation: The guide midpoint of $16.69 less the $2.98 of H1 gains disclosed in release footnote 3. No future gains are assumed.

Revenue grows about 10% to about $51B. The FY27 guide is $46.1-46.4B, but the Q3 guide of 11-12% includes slightly above 4pts from Informatica, so organic growth is only about 7-8%. Contentful and Fin add inorganic revenue in FY28. Non-GAAP margin rises from 34.3% to about 34.8-35.0%, so operating income grows about 11-12%. Interest on the March-2026 notes is mostly in the Q2 run-rate ($473M/qtr), but Q1 FY27 carried only a partial quarter, and about $5.1B of deal cash stops earning interest. Together these cost about 1-2pts of net income growth. Cut from round 1's implied +12%.

Q2 diluted shares were 821M. 103M were delivered under the ASR at $198.34 (about 80%). $25B at the $182 expected average (Investor Day slide 25) is about 137M in total, so about 34M arrive at the October settlement, leaving about 787M. Only a slow resumption of net buybacks is assumed (about 0.5% average effect in FY28) because about $5.1B of cash goes to Contentful and Fin. Round 1 used 775M.
$12.6B / 783M = $16.1-16.3. That is near the FY28 consensus of about $16.0 (StockAnalysis aggregator) and in line with the supervisor's stress case. Round 1 had $16.7.

Net income +11% (revenue about +10% toward the $63B+ FY30 target on slide 26, which includes M&A; margin +50bp; interest flat) plus about 1.5% net buyback shrink. The ASR benefit is not counted again; it is already in FY28.
Salesforce's fiscal year ends Jan 31, so the NTM window at 2027-09-30 is about 4 months of FY28 plus 8 months of FY29: 1/3 x 16.3 + 2/3 x 18.4 = $17.7. Round 1's $18.3 overweighted FY29.

Today CRM trades at about 15x NTM core EPS (231 / about 15.3), against about 10x at the June-2026 trough and 20-30x historically. I hold about 14.5x: no rerating until the December print shows organic reacceleration, and leverage is higher after the debt-funded ASR.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM (Sep-2027) FCF of about $17.3B (1/3 FY28 $16.2B + 2/3 FY29 $17.8B), less SBC of about $4.8B (about 9% of NTM revenue of about $54B), gives about $12.5B. Over 783M shares that is $16.0/share, at a 6.25% SBC-adjusted equity FCF yield.

inputs_detail.derivation: FY28 +8%: operating income +11-12%, less a full year of cash interest on the $25B of notes (10-Q debt table); capex about 1.5% of revenue per guidance. FY29 +10%, with interest flat.

inputs_detail.value: about 9.0% of revenue (FY27 about $4.2B, $4.96/share); NTM about $4.8B
inputs_detail.derivation: The FY27 GAAP-to-non-GAAP margin bridge shows SBC at 9.0%. I hold about 9% on NTM revenue of about $54B, a little below 9% for FY29. Round 1 capitalized pre-SBC FCF; the supervisor flagged that my pre-SBC 7.75% yield was equivalent to about 5.5% SBC-adjusted.
The same post-ASR bridge as the P/E method.

The current SBC-adjusted yield on FY27 is about 5.9% (($15.0B - $4.2B) / about 790M / $231). I apply a slightly higher 6.25% 12 months out for leverage (about $39B of debt) and the unresolved seat-erosion risk. That is a touch below the 6.4-6.5% other forecasters used, because the market is paying about 5.9% today.

bear.story: The December Q3 print shows no organic reacceleration (organic stays about 7% or lower, cRPO slows to high single digits), and seat compression shows up in Sales and Service Cloud renewals. Agentforce ARR, now more broadly defined (it includes Slackbot and Headless 360), stops convincing. Engineering-leadership turnover (the Tallapragada transition) slows delivery. The multiple falls to about 10x on about $16 core EPS, and the $182 ASR is underwater on about $39B of debt.

base.story: Revenue grows about 10% with cRPO at 12-14%, the margin edges up to about 35%, and the post-ASR share count of about 783-787M lifts FY28 core EPS to about $16.3 and NTM EPS to about $17.7. The multiple stays about 14x while the AI-disruption debate stays unresolved.

bull.story: Agentforce and Data 360 ARR goes from about $3.9B to $7B+, NNAOV strength (a four-year high) converts into 10%+ organic growth, and the market rerates CRM toward about 19x on NTM EPS of about $18.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $163 (about 10x FY28 core EPS of about $16.3, around the 2026 trough zone of $146-178), the market would be pricing an actual seat-base decline or a failed H2 organic reacceleration, contradicting management's 'on track for second-half organic revenue reacceleration' and the Q3 cRPO guide of about 14%. It would also put the $182-average ASR underwater on about $39B of debt. A move there would most likely reflect a fundamental miss (a cRPO or FY28 guide cut, visible net seat losses, or failed integration of Informatica, Fin or Contentful) and not 47%-vol noise. Lowered from $165 because FY28 EPS was revised down.

reasoning: Primary documents show a business growing about 11% reported (about 7-8% organic once more than 4pts of Informatica are stripped out), with cRPO guided at about 14%, NNAOV at a four-year high and Agentforce plus Data 360 ARR near $3.9B (definition widened in Q2). FY27 core EPS excluding the $2.98 of H1 investment gains is about $13.7. The supervisor's review corrected two things in my round-1 build. First, Sep-2027 NTM EPS must blend 1/3 FY28 and 2/3 FY29. Second, my FY28 of $16.7 on 775M shares assumed buybacks resume too fast while $5.1B goes to Contentful and Fin. I re-derived FY28 at about $16.3 (core net income +10% on about 783M shares, near the $16.0 consensus) and FY29 at about $18.4, which gives NTM about $17.7. At 14.5x that is $257. I also re-checked the Q2 release, which confirms SBC at 9.0% of revenue, and switched the FCF method to SBC-adjusted: $16.0/share at 6.25% gives $255. The blended fair value is $256 (from $266). I stay slightly above the supervisor's $251 because the market already pays about 5.9% SBC-adjusted FCF and about 15x core EPS today, and I see no reason to demand a higher yield than the current one plus a small leverage premium. Scenarios: bear $160 (23%, raised from 22% for the leadership transition and the thin organic growth), base $250 (52%), bull $340 (25%). Base rates: large caps move ±25-35% a year, and CRM's realized vol is 47%. The ladder is a 77/23 mixture of a lognormal (median $258, sigma 0.315) and a bear lognormal (median $170, sigma 0.30). That gives P(>= today's $231) of about 0.53, a price-only mean of about $250 and a fat left tail. Round-2 research was one primary-document re-check (the Q2 8-K exhibit); option data and priors were not consulted.
